clips.text: [warm, conversational] One useful correction can become something your coding agent remembers.
[concrete] You ask for the built-in case guard. The agent replaces the manual tag comparison in this edit.
anchors: You ask for the built-in case guard

clips.text: The agent reads your saved traits, then drafts a reusable rule: use case guards when testing or filtering tagged unions.
The draft goes to derive trait, which compares it with the collection. This example is a new preference, ready for your decision.
[inviting] You review the exact rule. Approve, edit, or skip. Here, you approve it. Nothing is saved before that choice.
anchors: Nothing is saved before that choice

clips.text: The approved rule becomes a Markdown file in your checkout. Its ID comes back to the agent, ready for future sessions.
Later, the agent sends new code to check traits. The model cross-references your rules and flags another manual comparison. The agent inspects the evidence.
anchors: sends new code to check traits

clips.text: [assured, not triumphant] The finding applies. The agent replaces the predicate with the guard, then reruns trait review and project checks. Model judgments are guidance, not guarantees.
anchors: replaces the predicate with the guard
reruns trait review and project checks

clips.text: [warm] Feedback becomes an approved rule. That rule helps improve the next edit, without relying on a half-remembered conversation.
anchors: without relying on a half-remembered conversation
